speaker: Doctor
text: I notice this is a newborn with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; can you tell me the baby's gestational age at birth and whether they have passed meconium within the first 48 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the newborn passed any meconium or stool since birth? Also, are you seeing any abdominal distension or tenderness on exam?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have not received confirmation on whether meconium has been passed or if the abdomen is distended, which are critical findings for this presentation. Given the bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance in a term newborn, I must rule out intestinal obstruction immediately. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal X-ray findings demonstrate a 'double bubble' sign, which is indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "double bubble" sign on your X-ray strongly suggests duodenal atresia, which explains the bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. To confirm this diagnosis and check for any associated anomalies, I will now order an ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "double bubble" sign on the X-ray is highly specific for duodenal atresia, so the normal ultrasound likely just means there are no associated anomalies like renal issues or a second atresia. Since the radiographic evidence is classic and the clinical picture fits perfectly, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia
